findings.public_requirement: A transistor-level AGC amplifier and manual or automatic gain selector must produce agc and select mgc or agc onto gc according to mc.
findings.electrical_reason: The detector-to-AGC inputs are exclusively AC coupled by Caga and Cagb. At the detector's rectified/averaged DC error output, these capacitors are open, while Ragbp and Ragbn force both AGC input bases to vref13. Consequently the active differential pair and follower establish only a quiescent agc value independent of the detector amplitude; no DC detector-error control path exists to drive automatic gain control. The reported zero AGC gain is consistent with this disconnection. The transmission-gate selector is electrically valid, but it merely selects this nonresponsive agc node in automatic mode.

findings.public_requirement: The required TIA, two RF stages, output buffer, detector, AGC, and selector must form a complete receiver whose finalp and finaln outputs meet the nominal, overload, power, and PAM4 requirements.
findings.electrical_reason: Although the forward TIA-to-output chain is connected, the required automatic control path is not physically coherent for the detector's averaged output: Caga and Cagb block the detector DC response and Ragbp/Ragbn rebias both AGC inputs to vref13. Thus agc cannot convey detector amplitude to the automatic selector devices XMngc/XMpgc2 and gc, leaving the detector/AGC feedback portion of the claimed complete receiver functionally disconnected.

summary: The input TIA/cancellation, two gc-controlled RF stages, active output buffer, and active detector are genuinely implemented and connected. The AGC amplifier lacks a DC path from the rectified detector outputs, so automatic detector-based gain control and therefore the full closed receiver control path are not implemented.
